title: Assuming one success transfers unchanged across the company or portfolio
summary: Reuse proven assets while revalidating local workflows, data, economics, authority and adoption.
diagnosis: A successful implementation provides a useful starting point, not a universal template. Another company may have different definitions, exceptions, system access, review capacity or customer expectations. Separate the reusable technical and learning assets from assumptions that were local to the first setting. Scale through evidence about the new context rather than through executive enthusiasm alone.
diagnostic_questions: Which parts of the original success depended on local data, people, incentives or system architecture?
What is genuinely reusable, and what must be re-specified or tested in the new setting?
Does the second organisation have the ownership and support capacity required to sustain the approach?
proposed_actions: Package reusable components with their scope, assumptions, tests, known failures and operating requirements—not only code or a success story.
Run a local fit assessment and bounded validation using the receiving team’s cases, definitions, permissions and baseline.
Share failures and adaptations across the portfolio, then revise the common pattern without forcing every business into identical work practices.
working_artifact: Transfer assessment: original use case; evidence and limitations; reusable assets; local differences; data/definitions; authority; economics; adoption; support; new tests; acceptance owner; scale decision.
measures: Local accepted-task performance and business outcome relative to that organisation’s own baseline.
Adaptation and support cost per receiving business, including changes to definitions and permissions.
Reuse that reduces delivery effort without increasing unresolved exceptions, local workarounds or shared failure exposure.
tradeoff: The corpus contains many first-party cases and strategic proposals, not a validated universal transformation blueprint. Shared context and tooling can also propagate a common error widely. Keep local boundaries, test important differences and retain a way to stop a problematic shared release.
illustrative_case: Illustrative application: an agent that works for one distributor encounters different pack sizes, substitution rules and customer contracts in another. Reusing the test method and connectors may help; copying the policy assumptions unchanged may fail.
